version.changelog:
Initial release of ClawSentry.

- Installs and configures security-related plugins required by OpenClaw, including ai-assistant-security-openclaw.
- Provides a step-by-step process for script execution, login URL extraction, and user notification.
- Includes a 10-minute monitoring protocol for the plugin’s login process.
- Ensures strict order and verification for installation and setup steps.

llm.summary: The skill's steps broadly match an installer/login flow, but it includes an opaque bundled JavaScript file from an unknown source and instructs the agent to read and re-run local tokens/processes—behaviors that are plausible for setup but also risk-sensitive and not fully justified by the metadata.

dimensions.detail: The name/description claim to install security plugins and the runtime instructions (run a Node script, produce a login URL, read .state/login_state.json) are coherent with that purpose. However the skill includes an executable, minified bundle.js with no source or homepage; that reduces provenance and makes the inclusion disproportionate to a simple installer-written SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to execute a local Node script, read {baseDir}/.state/login_state.json (including loginToken and deviceFingerprint), monitor a process every minute and restart it with tokens if necessary. Those instructions grant the agent the ability to read local state and invoke/restart processes and rely on command-line passing of tokens—actions that go beyond a passive installer flow and could expose sensitive tokens or allow unintended process control.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external install spec, but the skill ships a minified/packed scripts/bundle.js and requires executing it. Running opaque bundled code from an unknown source is high-risk because its full behavior (network endpoints, exfiltration, privilege use) is not clear from metadata or SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, which is appropriate, but its runtime instructions read local state files that contain loginToken/deviceFingerprint and pass them on the command line to restart processes. Reading and reusing local tokens and device identifiers is plausible for login flows but is sensitive: tokens on command lines are exposed to other local processes and may be exfiltrated by the bundle. No justification or provenance for these sensitive reads is provided.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request permanent platform-wide presence. The demanded monitoring is time-limited (10 minutes) and self-contained to the skill's scripts, so there is no explicit persistent privilege escalation in the manifest.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill will execute an included, minified Node script from an unknown source and instruct the agent to read local state (loginToken/deviceFingerprint), monitor and restart processes. That behavior could be legitimate for a plugin login flow but is also sensitive. Before installing: (1) Confirm the publisher/source and prefer an official release URL/checksum; (2) inspect the full script for network endpoints and data exfiltration (or run it in an isolated VM/container); (3) avoid exposing tokens on command lines—review login_state.json contents first; (4) consider running the installer manually yourself rather than allowing an automated agent to execute it; (5) if you cannot verify provenance or fully review the bundle, do not run it on a production machine.
llm.findings:
[uses_child_process_exec_execSync] expected: The bundled script clearly requires child_process and calls exec/execSync to obtain a machine id and run system commands. This is expected for collecting a device fingerprint, but executing shell commands in bundled, opaque code increases risk.
[uses_crypto_hashing] expected: The bundle uses crypto.createHash to hash machine identifiers (likely to create deviceFingerprint). This is consistent with a login/device-fingerprint flow but is sensitive because the hashed value can be tied to the machine.
[opaque_minified_bundle] unexpected: The script is bundled/minified and lacks a clear source URL or homepage; that is not expected for a security plugin installer where provenance is important.
